title_en: Letter of the Churches of Lyons and Vienne
author: Churches of Lyons and Vienne
addressee: the brothers in Asia and Phrygia who hold the same faith and hope
occasion: Christians at Vienne and Lyons have suffered exclusion, arrest, torture and death in a civic persecution. They write to fellow Christians in Asia and Phrygia to report the scale of the affliction and the endurance of the martyrs.
argument: The assault comes from the Adversary, who trains his own people against the servants of God, while God's grace sets firm pillars who draw his attack onto themselves and count suffering small beside the coming glory. After mob abuse and imprisonment, Vettius Epagathus joins the martyrs, some weak Christians lapse, and arrested household slaves falsely accuse Christians of Thyestean feasts and Oedipodean unions, making hatred worse. Sanctus, Maturus, Attalus and especially the enslaved Blandina endure tortures beyond description without yielding, Sanctus answering only I am a Christian and being miraculously healed for a second torture, while the lapsed Biblis revives under torture, denies the slanders and confesses. Prison hardships, the beating and death of the aged bishop Pothinus, and the visible contrast between joyful confessors and shamed deniers confirm the faithful and warn against denial.

outline.move: Greeting from the servants of Christ who sojourn in Vienne and Lyons in Gaul to the brothers in Asia and Phrygia.

General account of the Adversary's attack, exclusion from public places, mob violence, examination before civic authorities, and imprisonment until the governor arrives, met by God's grace and steadfast endurance.
Vettius Epagathus offers to defend the brothers, is asked only whether he is a Christian, confesses, and is taken into the number of the martyrs.

The rest are sorted into ready first-martyrs and about ten unprepared who lapse, new arrests fill their number, and frightened pagan household slaves falsely accuse Christians of cannibal feasts and incest.

The full wrath of mob, governor and soldiers falls on Sanctus the deacon from Vienne, Maturus the newly baptized contender, Attalus of Pergamene origin, and Blandina, whose weakness becomes strength, plus Sanctus's sole answer and burning plates, his later healing, and the lapsed Biblis's repentance and confession.

The devil invents prison miseries in darkness and stretching of feet in the stocks to the fifth hole, most are suffocated in prison as the Lord wills it, the previously tortured are sustained by the Lord and encourage others, while the young newly arrested whose bodies had not been worn down by torture cannot bear the confinement and die inside.
The more-than-ninety-year-old bishop Pothinus of Lyons is dragged to the tribunal, answers the governor about the Christians' God, is beaten by the crowd, and dies in prison after two days.

God's ordering is shown in the double punishment and shame of the deniers contrasted with the joy, beauty and fragrance of the confessors, strengthening those later arrested to confess without hesitation.

cast.name: Vettius Epagathus
cast.who: A young but eminent Christian who volunteers to defend the brothers and becomes a martyr.

cast.name: Sanctus
cast.who: Deacon from Vienne who endures extreme torture answering only in Latin that he is a Christian.

cast.name: Maturus
cast.who: A newly baptized but brave contender, named with Sanctus, Attalus and Blandina as objects of the full wrath of mob, governor and soldiers.

cast.name: Attalus
cast.who: A man of Pergamene origin described as a pillar and support of the local Christians.

cast.name: Blandina
cast.who: An enslaved Christian woman whose endurance despite bodily weakness becomes the central proof of Christ's power.

cast.name: Biblis
cast.who: One of those who first denied the faith but repents under torture and joins the martyrs.

cast.name: Pothinus
cast.who: Bishop of Lyons, over ninety and infirm, beaten at the tribunal and dead in prison after two days.

cast.name: Zacharias
cast.who: The elder Zacharias, whose witness Vettius though young was held equal to; the blameless walk is said of Vettius, who is said to have in himself the Paraclete, the spirit of Zacharias.

voices.speaker: The Lord
voices.how_marked: introduced as what was spoken by our Lord, then a prediction that killers will think they offer worship to God

voices.speaker: Blandina
voices.how_marked: direct declaration in torture, introduced as her saying: I am a Christian and nothing base happens among us

voices.speaker: Sanctus
voices.how_marked: repeated answer to every interrogation in Latin: I am a Christian, heard as his only word

voices.speaker: Biblis
voices.how_marked: retort to the blasphemers under torture about eating children when even animal blood is forbidden

voices.speaker: Pothinus
voices.how_marked: answer to the governor's question who is the God of the Christians: If you are worthy, you will know

scripture: No book names, authors, or Psalm numbers are given in sections 1-13; sayings are woven in without citation, except one introduced as spoken by our Lord. _unresolved_facts.fix: Say that the names of the governor (ἡγεμών), the chiliarch (χιλίαρχος, 'tribune') and the city authorities are not given. Their offices are named in sections 4, 5 and 12.

_unresolved_facts.claim: They write to fellow Christians in Asia and Phrygia to report the scale of the affliction and the endurance of the martyrs.

_unresolved_facts.fix: The writers say they cannot give the full size of the affliction and the martyrs' sufferings exactly, or capture it in writing. Rephrase as 'to give an account of the affliction and the martyrs' endurance, which they say cannot be fully told'.
